title: KitchenAid Expandable Stainless Steel Colander, One size, Black
description:
About this item
DRAIN & RINSE WITH EASE: this Over-the-Sink strainer/colander is perfect for straining, draining, rinsing pastas, fruits and vegetables over the sink
STAINLESS STEEL: crafted from stainless steel, this strainer has a plastic trim with non-slip rubber encased handles that expand to securely fit across almost any size sink
NON SLIP FEET: the rubber encased feet Let the strainer sit inside your sink or on your counter without slipping or scratching
MEASURES: The strainer measures 16-inches and fully expanded, it measure 22-inches
EASY TO CLEAN: Dishwasher safe for fast and easy cleanup
› See more product details
reviews_5s:
We have a big family, easily handles 2 lbs of pasta.
Doesn’t fall over if you pour too fastThis was a great gift when we received it some years ago. The sliding arms let you position it over your sink and easily drain your pasta or veggies or whatever. Cleans up easily, stores handily with the sliding arms retracted. Sadly, I didn’t read the directions that came with it and lazily placed it in the dishwasher. Turns out the metal in the sliding arms (not the mesh) isn’t dishwasher safe. Alas, our lovely little gift was ruined. ☹️ Quick, search Amazon! Tah-dah! OXO still makes the same sieve basket. Click, and we’re back in business.So far so good. I love that it extends across the sink and it’s very sturdy. It’s a bit heavy and cumbersome to clean, but I’m happy with it. It’s very sturdy and well made, and is a generous size. It solves the problem with drain water coming up through other stand up strainers. I’d definitely recommend it.A kitchen must. I do not risk burning myself now, easy to clean, and easy to set up.Ever have a large pot of pasta and need to drain the water? You set a colander down in the sink and it's difficult to reach down there and the steam gets hot and splashes? This nice, deep strainer stretches across most standard kitchen sinks and allows easy access and gives you safe handles to pick it up after to return the pasta, rice, etc. to your cook pot or sauce. Plus we all know you can never have enough colanders and strainers if you cook and bake a lot.I purchased this sink basket to replace my previous one. It fits perfect in my sink. Very sturdy and looks nice. I use it everyday.This item is absolutely fantastic. I keep it in my double sink, on one side, Use it when I make salads, and when I peel my vegetables to wash them before I get them in the pot to boil.Arrived on time in excellent condition and exactly what I ordered.Don’t wait..
Do yourself a favor and order this jewel. Expandable so fits any sink. Large capacity and food does not fall through. Very good buy for many purposes.This is great for my double sink, but you want to check the measurements before using it on a single large/farm style sink. It's bulky but it's a perfect replacement for my old plastic colander with large holes.
reviews_1s:
With the brand name you would THINK...ok....should be a good product. SO.......I know, I know.....my fault for NOT triple checking the sizing on this thing. I focused on the length it would take to fit across the sink. Wrong focus!!! It's well made and very sturdy BUT.....the actual colander part of the strainer is about as big as a cereal bowl. TINY!!!!!!!! While it's true that the "arms" reach across your sink, if you have to strain anything more than ONE large potato or a very few strands of pasta, go with another item. This over-the-sink strainer part MIGHT could hold 1 can of say....chickpeas or something. Get you to buy the brand name rip-off if ever there was. Don't do what I did and not pay attention to the actual dimensions of the colander portion. DO NOT waste your money on this strainer, unless of course you want a miniscule colander.I purchased because I appreciate the quality of a steel strainer instead of a plastic one, and the description said dishwasher safe. it's not dishwasher safe--the main components are, but the screws for the retractable arms are not and after a single wash they were already way rusted. now I can't put in the dishwasher, which was the biggest feature I bought it for. poorly designed product; if one component isn't dishwasher safe, the whole thing isn't dishwasher safe.I bought this due to it saying that you can put it in the dishwasher. The package says to hand wash.The problem is that the cheap plastic that holds in the sliding side arms broke apart, and now one of the arms easily comes out of the colander. No easy way to fix. Kitchenaid ain't what it use to be.When I took this out of the package it was rusted - it came off easily so I threw it in the dishwasher and it was very rusted when it came out. I towel dried it and still MORE RUST

it would be really great without the rust aspect…expect way more from kitchen aid brand.Sturdy and I loved it, until I noticed the rust. It’s not the mesh, but the metal frame and arms that are rusting. So are the screws that help lock the arms back in. This will fall apart in a few weeks for sure.Item seemed to function well, but covered in rust within a month. hard tp figure for an item that's obviously meant to be wet. Maybe KitchenAid hasn't heard of the new fangled creation called stainless steel?Broke within six months after using it a few times. Used primarily outside the dishwasher and the handles just gave up.This item immediately broke upon my first time using it. Only one of the arms extends all the way out. I expected better from kitchenaid.Became rusted after about ten times usage.
Additionally, the plastic is broken
